calls.title: Open Call – BBA Artist Prize 2026
calls.description: We invite artists from around the world to apply for the BBA Artist Prize 2026. All mediums and themes are welcome, and the competition is open to anyone 18+, regardless of experience, education, or background.
calls.requirements: open to anyone 18+, regardless of experience, education, or background.

calls.title: Demos
calls.description: The aim with Demos is to facilitate networks and meetings between civil society organisations in the Nordics. A strong and dynamic civil society is a cornerstone of Nordic democracy. The funding programme promotes the ability of stakeholders in Nordic civil society to work together, to influence, and to strengthen their voice. The partnerships will help the Nordic Region on its way to becoming the most sustainable and integrated region in the world by 2030.
calls.requirements:
Please note that only civil society organisations can apply for funding.

Funding can be applied for by non-profit civil society organisations in all areas of society . These organisations include associations, foundations, charities, citizens organisations, interest groups, labour market organisations, religious communities, social enterprises, and NGOs. Demos funds projects with participation from at least three (3) different Nordic countries. Denmark, the Faroe Islands, Finland, Greenland, Iceland, Norway, Sweden, and Åland are considered as separate countries in this context. To be eligible, the applicant organisation must be established and registered in the Nordic Region. Denmark, the Faroe Islands, Finland, Greenland, Iceland, Norway, Sweden, and Åland are considered as Nordic countries in this context. Although the project may cover additional partners who do not operate in the Nordic Region, at least three Nordic countries must be represented. The partner is considered to represent the country or area in which the organisation is registered. The organisation and partners must have a democratic structure and operations. The organisation and partners must not pursue making a profit. The organisation must not owe taxes or fees to the state and must not have applied for bankruptcy or be in liquidation. Please note that individuals cannot apply for funding.

calls.description: Villa Arson and Université Côte d’Azur are offering a three-month photographic creation residency intended for a young photographer who has recently graduated or been recommended by a cultural or artistic structure, in response to the policy of support for emerging creation shared by the two institutions.

calls.title: SUSTAINED SUPPORT PROGRAMME FOR THE ARTS CROSS-DISCIPLINARY, CIRCUS, STREET ARTS AND DIGITAL ARTS (CREATION, EDITION, TRAINING, STRATEGIC MEDIATION ACTIONS)
calls.description: The Directorate-General for the Arts (DGARTES) makes public, through this notice, the opening of the competition for the submission of applications within the scope of the Sustained Support Program in the areas of Cross-disciplinary, Circus, Street Arts and Digital Arts, as provided for in Decree-Law No. 103/2017, of 24 August, in its current wording, and in the Regulation of the Arts Support Programs, approved in annex to Ordinance No. 345-A/2026/1, of 14 August, under the following terms:
calls.requirements:
1. Private legal persons with headquarters in Portugal, who here carry out, on a predominant basis, professional activities in one or more of the artistic areas provided for in Article 1(2) of Decree-Law No. 103/2017, of 24 August, in its current wording, according to the following access conditions: a) Biennial support modality: have at least four years of continuous professional activity; b) Quadriennial support modality: have at least six years of continuous professional activity; have benefited, at least once in the last six years, from State financial support through DGARTES under the sustained support typology, provided that the sanction provided for in point c) of paragraph 1 of Article 23 has not been applied to them, nor is the sanction provided for in point a) of paragraph 1 of the same article being applied, regardless of their legal nature or institutional model; have a creation and/or presentation space suitable for pursuing the supported activity.

2. For the purposes of access to the modality provided for in point b) of paragraph 1, the last two cycles of sustained support (2018-2022 and 2023-2026), in the quadriennial and biennial modality, awarded under Decree-Law No. 103/2017, of 24 August, in its current wording, are considered.
3. Private foundations or private law public foundations that have another type of continuous funding, ensured by the budget programme of the culture area, as well as associations made up mostly of public entities and companies in the state business sector and of the autonomous regions, are not admitted to the tender procedure.
4. Entities that have signed an addendum to renew the sustained support contract in the quadriennial modality are not admitted to the tender procedure.
5. Entities must frame their activity in only one application and, in the event of support being granted, the respective contract constitutes the sole support instrument for the period for which it is intended, except as provided for in Article 26(4) of Decree-Law No. 103/2017, of 24 August, in its current wording.

calls.title: New Norwegian fiction for adults – automatic acquisition scheme
calls.description: The scheme shall contribute to new Norwegian fiction for adults being created, published, distributed and read.
calls.requirements: Publishers and other publishers with a Norwegian organisation number can submit books to this scheme. It is not possible to submit books to both the automatic and the selective acquisition scheme for new Norwegian fiction for the same target group within the same publication year. It is important that you as the publisher have entered into an agreement with the author and any other rights holders (such as illustrators or translators) before you apply. The Arts Council of Norway can decide that a publisher is not allowed to submit books for a period if they have not complied with the conditions for the scheme previously. For example, this may be because the publisher has not repaid money by the stated deadlines. Remember that an author can usually only have one book for adults and one book for children and young people submitted to the acquisition schemes for fiction each calendar year. This is called the “one-book rule.” The one-book rule applies to this scheme and the selective acquisition scheme for fiction for adults together. This means that the author cannot have more than one book submitted to the acquisition schemes for fiction for adults in the same year. You can apply for an exemption from the one-book rule on behalf of the author. You must do this before the first book is published. The application must be justified. The book must be new Norwegian fiction for adults. By fiction we mean novels, short stories, short prose, poetry, drama and picture books. Under this scheme, we classify drama in metrical form as poetry. We also classify books with mainly fact-based and professional content as fiction if the books have a sufficiently literary character. The book must either be written in Norwegian (Bokmål, Nynorsk or dialect) or translated into Norwegian from Sámi or a national minority language or translated into Norwegian from another language if it is an original work that has not been published previously, or a translation of poetry into Norwegian. By new we mean that the book is published as an original work in the same year that you apply. Translations of poetry into Norwegian are considered new literary works. Collections of poems and short stories are considered new if less than half of the content has been printed previously. In any case, the collection must be assessed as a unified literary work. If the author of the book is deceased, you can apply for up to five years after the author passed away. If the book is translated from Sámi or a national minority language, the original work cannot be more than five years old when you apply.

calls.title: Independent performing arts – project (theatre)

Private individuals, private and public institutions, organizations, and other businesses may apply. Applicants who receive fixed annual state grants are normally not awarded grants from this scheme.

calls.requirements: Professionally producing artists/groups from the independent performing arts (including performance, drama, dance, music theater, puppet and object theater, theater in public space, contemporary circus) based and working in Germany.

calls.organisation: Czech Centre Brussels, Kunstfort Vijfhuizen, EUNIC Netherlands, Zoöp, and DutchCulture
calls.description: This residency and open call have been developed in collaboration with the Czech Centre Brussels, Kunstfort Vijfhuizen, EUNIC Netherlands, Zoöp, and DutchCulture, and are intended for artists, researchers, and creative practitioners with a connection to the Czech Republic or Czech cultural practice.

Residents may come from a wide range of creative fields, including visual arts, design, research, literature, performance, music, technology, or other interdisciplinary practices.

calls.title: Sustained Support Programme for the Arts – Music and Opera (Creation, Publishing, Training, Strategic Mediation Actions)
calls.description: The Directorate-General for the Arts (DGARTES) hereby makes public, through this notice, the opening of the call for the submission of applications under the Sustained Support Programme in the area of Music and Opera, pursuant to Decree-Law No. 103/2017, of 24 August, in its current wording, and the Regulation of the Arts Support Programmes, approved in annex to Ministerial Order No. 345-A/2026/1, of 14 August, under the following terms:
calls.requirements:
1. Private legal entities with registered office in Portugal, which carry out, on a predominant basis, professional activities in one or more of the artistic areas provided for in Article 1(2) of Decree-Law No. 103/2017 of 24 August, as currently amended, under the following access conditions: a) Biennial support modality: have at least four years of continuous professional activity; b) Quadriennial support modality: have at least six years of continuous professional activity; have benefited, at least once in the last six years, from financial support from the State through DGARTES under the sustained support type, provided that they have not been subject to the sanction provided for in point c) of paragraph 1 of Article 23, nor is the sanction provided for in point a) of paragraph 1 of the same article being applied, regardless of their legal nature or institutional model; have suitable creation and/or presentation space for the pursuit of the supported activity.

2. For the purposes of access to the modality provided for in point b) of paragraph 1, the last two sustained support cycles (2018-2022 and 2023-2026), in the quadriennial and biennial modalities, granted under Decree-Law No. 103/2017 of 24 August, as currently amended, are considered.
3. Private foundations or private-law public foundations that have other types of continuous funding, ensured by the budget programme of the culture area, as well as associations mainly constituted by public entities and companies in the State enterprise sector and in the autonomous regions, are not admitted to the tender procedure.
4. Entities that have signed an addendum renewing the sustained support contract in the quadriennial modality are not admitted to the tender procedure.
5. Entities must frame their activity in only one application and, in the event of the granting of support, the respective contract constitutes the sole support instrument for the period to which it is intended, except as provided for in Article 26(4) of Decree-Law No. 103/2017 of 24 August, as currently amended.

calls.title: MOBILITY Program 2026 FIRST SESSION
calls.description: The Mobility Program 2026 is aimed at providing financial support to Bulgarian cultural organizations, individual artists and creative groups for participation in international cultural and educational forums in Bulgaria and abroad, with the aim of further development and creation of international contacts and partnerships.

calls.title: 1.4.1 Creation and realization of works – fine and visual art
calls.description: Subprogram 1.4 – Fine and visual art is focused on supporting professional art (classical media, new media, photography, design and architecture) with the aim of maintaining the continuity of fine and visual culture, supporting the creation of new artistic forms and activities of a non-commercial character.

The applicant must have one of the following legal forms: a) budgetary organization or contributory organization founded by a higher territorial unit, b) budgetary organization or contributory organization founded by a municipality, c) non-profit organization providing generally beneficial services, d) commercial company, e) civic association, f) non-investment fund, g) foundation, h) association of legal persons with a special interest.

calls.title: Open Call Choreographic Encounters
calls.organisation: Dansateliers and choreographer Amparo González Sola
calls.description: Dansateliers and choreographer Amparo González Sola invite choreographers to apply for the first edition of the Choreographic Encounters Laboratory. This edition will explore choreographic procedures and strategies of attention in a peer-to-peer environment.
calls.requirements:
Who can apply? The application is open to artists with a grounded artistic movement practice and an established body of work. Artists are interested in choreographic procedures, tools and audience strategies in relation to their own work. They have experience with peer-to-peer feedback and are interested in and comfortable with sharing their practice and work with others. Please note: We are open to artists with specific access needs. The Dansateliers building is currently not wheelchair accessible. Participants need to be able to climb stairs to reach the studios.

We are looking for
• 1 artist residing in Europe
• 1 artist residing in The Netherlands
